A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same attention-geometry and Active Subspace Initialization study. All pages, including appendices, equations, tables, and figures, support comparison; relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: V1 reports original activation-spectrum analyses, SAE initialization and scaling experiments, and a Lorsa initialization comparison.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds residual-stream, JumpReLU, annealed-TopK, and expanded Lorsa experiments.

M1.justification: The core SAE initializer remains unchanged, but Section 5.4 substantially revises its Lorsa adaptation: v1 initializes output weights and explicitly lacks encoder alignment; v2 uses per-original-head active subspaces and aligns encoder weights with corresponding input directions. Appendix H.1 also proposes staged PCA-space training followed by projection folding for high-l0 warm-up.

E1.justification: The model families, corpora, English/code/Chinese coverage, and attention/MLP/residual activation domains are retained. Residual-stream activations already appear in v1's spectral and LlamaScope evaluations. V2's additional ASI and SAE-variant experiments deepen testing within this existing data and task coverage.

E2.justification: V2 adds base JumpReLU and Pre-Act Loss comparisons in Figures 13–14, plus TopK Anneal in Figure 15. The existing TopK, AuxK, SparseAdam variants, and vanilla Lorsa comparisons remain. Random-subspace initialization is retained in Appendix B.1, having appeared in v1 Figure 5.

E3.justification: V2 introduces low-l0 versus warm-up JumpReLU protocols, annealed-TopK tests, and Lorsa comparisons at five layer-depth fractions. Section 4.2 changes spectral and loss-recovery reporting thresholds from 5% to 1% and 95% to 99%. Figure 2's caption changes 1M samples to 10M tokens, although v1 Appendix B already stated 10M; this does not establish a rerun.

E4.justification: Appendices B and H add substantive tests of ASI's limits on near-full-rank residual activations, JumpReLU warm-up regimes, and annealed TopK. The existing initialization-dimension/random-subspace analysis gains downstream-loss measurements, and Figure 6 adds dead-feature rates across sparsity levels. Existing variance-threshold sensitivity plots are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty bars. Additional curves do not introduce a new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: V1 Table 1's Lorsa results—68.4% versus 40.5% dead parameters and 0.130 versus 0.121 normalized MSE—are replaced by multi-layer results for the revised initializer in v2 Figure 8, preventing a direct same-setting comparison. V2 adds residual-stream and JumpReLU findings, additional metric curves, and worse ASI performance under TopK annealing in Figure 15. Figure 7's scaling results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The attention equations, SVD-based intrinsic-dimension definition, variance decomposition, and subspace-dimension argument are retained. Expanded matrix descriptions and implementation pseudocode do not add or revise formal theoretical results.

C1.justification: The abstract softens low-rankness from a 'fundamental cause' to a 'key factor' in dead features. The main claims about attention-output geometry, output-projection anisotropy, ASI, and reducing dead features from 87% to below 1% remain; the conclusion still uses causal language.

C2.justification: New Section 6 explicitly acknowledges that the causal mechanism remains unclear and limits expected benefits for near-full-rank activations. Appendices B.3, G.4, and H add explanations involving insufficient subspace coverage and feature-direction drift during high-l0 training, together with practical applicability qualifications.

D1.justification: V2 adds SAE/Lorsa pseudocode, decoder-norm grid-search details, ordinary-training learning rate and batch size, and the scaling learning-rate schedule. It also documents JumpReLU configurations, a 1M-token downstream-loss evaluation, and 5-sigma activation filtering. These are substantial reporting additions; newly disclosed settings do not establish changes to previously run experiments.

R1.justification: New Section 2.4 discusses PCA-inspired initialization, and the introduction explicitly credits Phan et al.'s PCsInit as inspiration. Supporting PCA, initialization, JumpReLU, and model references are added, while the existing related-work framework remains largely intact.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized rewrites, particularly in Sections 2.2, 5.2, and 5.4, adds a Discussion section, and reorganizes the training appendices. It removes author-contribution statements and adds an LLM-use declaration. Most existing exposition and its sequence remain recognizable.

P2.justification: V2 changes the document template and opening illustration, fits the abstract onto the first page, converts Figure 1 to bars, and splits Figure 4's overlaid axes into separate panels. Figures 5–6 gain panels, the Lorsa table becomes a multi-layer figure, and new appendix figures are added. Other appendix plots are merely relocated and renumbered.

improvement.justification: V2 provides better practical guidance through failure-condition tests that v1's broad applicability statements lacked, especially Appendices B and H. Added prior-work attribution and implementation details improve positioning and reproducibility information. These are clear gains, but the central causal account remains unresolved, and the conclusion retains stronger causal language than the new Discussion supports.
